title: #007. Worker-Task 1-to-1 Assignment
subtitle: Enforce exact row sums and column sums over a 0-1 decision matrix for minimum-cost matching.
markdown:
# #007. Worker-Task 1-to-1 Assignment

<!-- section:scenario -->
There are $n$ workers $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $n$ tasks $j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Assigning worker $i$ to task $j$ incurs cost `costs[i][j]`.

Find a **1-to-1 assignment** where every worker is assigned to **exactly one** task and every task is assigned to **exactly one** worker, minimizing total assignment cost.

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P007Input`)**: `costs: number[][]` — square $n \times n$ cost matrix
- **Output (`P007Output`)**:
  - `assignment: number[]` — array of length $n$ where `assignment[i]` is the task index $j$ given to worker $i$
  - `totalCost: number` — minimized $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \text{costs}[i][\text{assignment}[i]]$

<!-- section:example -->
With `costs = [[9, 2, 7], [6, 4, 3], [5, 8, 1]]`:

- **Worker-by-worker greedy**: Worker 0 picks Task 1 (`2`), Worker 1 picks Task 2 (`3`), forcing Worker 2 onto Task 0 (`5`) for `2 + 3 + 5 = 10`.
- **Optimal 1-to-1 matching**: Assigning `assignment = [1, 0, 2]` incurs `2 + 6 + 1 =` **`9`**!

<!-- section:hint1 -->
The 2D binary matrix `x[i][j]` (`n` rows by `n` columns) is declared in the starter code:
- **Row constraints** (each worker $i$ gets 1 task): `sum(x[i]) == 1`
- **Column constraints** (each task $j$ gets 1 worker): `sum(x.map((row) => row[j])) == 1`

<!-- section:hint2 -->
To build `assignment[i]` after `m.solve()` (`h.minimize(...)`), scan row `i` and pick the column index `j` where `Math.round(x[i][j].value!) === 1` (`round(h.val(x[i][j])) == 1` in Python).

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} c_{i,j} x_{i,j} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} x_{i,j} = 1 && \forall i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\} \\
& \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_{i,j} = 1 && \forall j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\} \\
& x_{i,j} \in \{0, 1\} && \forall i, j
\end{aligned}
$$

judge.m0: Output must be an object { assignment, totalCost }.
judge.m1: assignment[{p0}] must be an integer task index (received {p1}).
judge.m3: Task {p0} is assigned more than once — check your column-sum == 1 constraints.
judge.m4: Reported totalCost ({p0}) does not match computed cost sum ({p1}).
judge.m5: Valid 1-to-1 assignment, but totalCost ({p0}) exceeds optimal ({p1}).
